Definition: from G3192; relating to honey, i.e. bee (comb):--honeycomb.
BiblicalUsage: Melissios is the honeycomb, and its one place in the King James Bible is Luke 24:42, where the risen Jesus is given a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb. The Greek text behind the modern editions does not carry the word here, so the study rests on the King James reading alone.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the risen Christ eating with His friends is proof He was no spirit, and the honeycomb is part of that homely proof.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Appears to the Disciples on Easter Evening
